Parliament
National Assembly
Session: Twenty-first
Proceedings Summary
18 Jestha 2083
Monday
Meeting Number: 92
The National Assembly meeting today commenced at 13:22 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members,
(13:22 hrs)
Proceedings will commence. Please be seated, honourable members. Names have been received for speaking. I will call them in order. There is no tradition of standing up to speak. I will call names myself.
Honourable members, time has been requested for urgent matters. A maximum of three minutes has been allocated for speaking on urgent matters. I will now provide time to the honourable members in order. First, Honourable Member Ranjit Karna.
Honourable Mr. Ranjit Karna (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, yesterday (13:23 hrs) the Right Honourable Prime Minister himself stood at the Parliament's roster, at the House of Representatives' roster, and admitted that the Government of Nepal has encroached upon some lands of our neighbouring country, India. Through the Right Honourable Chairperson, I urge the Right Honourable Prime Minister to provide information within 24 hours about which areas of our neighbouring country India the Government of Nepal has encroached upon. Furthermore, if he cannot provide such information, he will have to publicly apologize to the public. Simultaneously, the Parliament of this National Assembly will have to make a special decision today. I demand today from the National Assembly that a committee be formed to investigate the reason behind what the Right Honourable Prime Minister said.
Concurrently, we have many queries for the Right Honourable Prime Minister here in the National Assembly. Because he is also a representative of the new generation, and after he presents the policy and program and budget, what he has addressed for the problems of that generation, for which lakhs of youth are currently going abroad, going out. I want to know.
Along with that, he spoke about the economic prosperity of Madhesh Province in Janakpur. The budget presented by the current Finance Minister states that Nepal's per capita income will be 1550 dollars in the future, whereas Madhesh Province's per capita income is only just over 1000 dollars. A deficit of 1000 dollars. For that Madhesh Province, whose economy is very weak. What has been addressed in the previous policy and program and budget? I urge him to come and answer all these matters while standing in the National Assembly. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.
(13:26 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepal Communist Party): Honourable Chairperson, for the first time in Nepal's history, we have heard someone publicly advocate for India from the Parliament of Nepal. I wish to draw the government's attention through the Right Honourable Chairperson to clarify on what basis Prime Minister Balendra Shah expressed this view and for the government to respond. I demand a response. Advocating for India from Nepal's Parliament is an act of treason. This issue does not belong to any particular political party; it is a matter of nationality. It is a matter of Nepal and the Nepali people. India has encroached upon approximately 62,000 hectares of Nepal's land, and it borders approximately 23 districts of Nepal. Various areas in the Terai have been encroached upon. Among these, we don't have to go too far. In Nawalparasi, 14,500 hectares of land in Susta has been encroached upon, and the people of Susta have repeatedly issued warnings. They have protected Nepal's land while being surrounded by India. We have been raising the issue of Susta since the student movement and through political parties for a long time. The issue of Kalapani and Lipulek is also being raised now. Therefore, when the Prime Minister of Nepal speaks in favour of India, is he trying to please India? We are in favour of the Government of Nepal continuing, not of the Government of Nepal collapsing. No one should try to erase Nepal's existence. We have heard every Nepali raise their voice in favour of Nepal while staying within the democratic republic and constitutional system brought about by the sacrifice of our martyrs and the struggle of the Nepali people, and every Nepali must raise this voice. Until a clear answer is received, we will continue to seek this answer. I wish to say this much. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri.
(13:29 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Ram Kumari Jhankri (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honourable Chairperson, the statement made yesterday by our country's Prime Minister, Mr. Balendra Shah, while addressing the House of Representatives has lowered the heads of self-respecting Nepalis. It has lowered the heads of patriotic citizens, causing shame. At such a time, there is not much more to say. Events and documents from many historical periods state that Nepal is a sovereign country, and its borders are mentioned in various historical documents. Even so, many years ago, all the border experts speaking today. The issue of border encroachment in about 62 places, when we entered student politics, we ourselves organized border security campaigns and messages for the motherland, and during such programs, those experts who are now talking about Buddhi Narayan Shrestha were on our team. They later wrote a book stating that the border has been encroached upon in 62 places. Not only has the border been encroached upon, but the presence of Indian armed forces has led to the beating of Nepalis. Govinda Gautam was even murdered in the Mahakali River. In such a situation, on the eve of the visit of the Chairperson of Rastriya Swatantra Party to India, with what intention did Prime Minister Balendra Shah come to the House of Representatives without prior notice, as if attending a concert, and speak to the MPs against the rules, saying he would answer? We do not believe this was a slip of the tongue or said carelessly. We believe there is some deeper reason behind it, and self-respecting Nepalis should take this seriously. It is not just about Susta Maheshpur; even today, armed Indian security forces are creating obstacles to the infrastructure being built in Susta. Therefore, when the citizens living on the border, the protectors of the border, are rendered helpless, the expert group formed between Nepal and India stated that there is border occupation. That occupation means that India has moved pillars at various times, moved the pillars, and Nepali land has been taken to the other side, and Nepal is cultivating its land. When Nepalis say the border has been encroached upon, in whose interest is the Prime Minister of Nepal acting? We are ashamed. The question also arises whether such a Prime Minister can protect Nepal's self-respect, nationality, and national integrity. For that reason, rather than the issue of apology or forgiveness, what is the Prime Minister's state of mind? We do not believe it was said carelessly, and what is this situation? Even as the Prime Minister is here, I want to tell the 30 million people, is it possible for such a traitorous Prime Minister to continue to be everyone's Prime Minister? (... Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma.
(13:32 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rastriya Janamorcha): Honourable Chairperson, today the heads of the Nepali people have been bowed by the statement made by the current Prime Minister yesterday. This is an extremely sad and shameful matter. We know that there has been a border dispute between Nepal and India for a long time. According to border expert Buddhi Narayan Shrestha, there is a border dispute in 72 places from Mechi to Mahakali along the Terai, in areas bordering India. The issues of Kalapani, Limpiyadhura, and Lipulek are repeatedly being raised. At such a time, the Prime Minister of the country has made a statement against his country's dignity and national interest. We express our regret for this. I also demand that he present evidence in this respected assembly about where Nepal has encroached upon India's border. I demand that he present it. Therefore, such activities by the country's top leader are not in the country's interest. It is against the interest of the constitution. Therefore, his expression against the country's dignity and nationality is objectionable, and how did he dare to speak like that? A person like the Prime Minister cannot possibly not know the country's history, the history of border disputes. He could have obtained information from his experts and his colleagues. But did he want to surrender to India? They have made various accusations against the previous government. They accused them of flattering foreigners, of being agents of foreigners, and some weaknesses and mistakes were made by previous governments. However, the current government, which came to power to correct them, has made this objectionable statement, which is anti-national. Therefore, I object to his statement. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the order of speaking during urgent time
(13:35 hrs)
ends here. (Voices of protest in the assembly) What is the matter again, honourable members?
You have expressed your protests during urgent time. What is the matter? Is there anything else you wish to raise? You have already raised that issue. Honourable ministers are present to represent the government. The feelings of all the honourable members present here, the views expressed, will certainly be conveyed to the relevant bodies by the honourable ministers. Therefore, honourable members, your feelings are of serious concern to me as well. The honourable members who raised the issues here, and I, from here, urge the honourable ministers of the Government of Nepal who are present here to convey all these matters to the concerned bodies. Therefore, honourable members, let us proceed with the proceedings. We have Zero Hour and Special Time according to our schedule. Please cooperate in moving forward. (Honourable members stand up from their seats and protest) Honourable members, please return to your seats and cooperate in conducting the assembly. Honourable members, I request again. Please cooperate in moving the assembly forward by returning to your seats. Your feelings can be expressed in other programs like Zero Hour. We can clearly express our feelings during Special Time as well, and these voices of protest, or what we are doing now, will certainly reach the Government of Nepal, and I expect that a response will definitely come from the Government of Nepal. Therefore, honourable members, let us sit down and cooperate in moving the proceedings forward. Again, it seems like a hundred percent protest.
(Sloganeering by honourable members)

Anti-national Prime Minister resign! Resign! Resign!
Long live national pride! Long live! Long live!
Uphold diplomatic dignity! Uphold! Uphold!
Honorable members, issues were raised earlier during the urgent time, and they were raised with seriousness. My serious attention has been drawn to these issues, and I believe the honorable ministers present from the Nepal government have also surely heard and taken this matter seriously. There was also some slogan shouting. This much is sufficient protest, in terms of legal procedures. Now, this kind of protest, this kind of feeling you have. The issues spoken by the Right Honorable Prime Minister yesterday are not something that can be resolved today. It is also something that can continue in the coming days. Therefore, honorable members, let us stop the current process of protest here and cooperate in conducting the assembly. We have established a standard that in the National Assembly, we have raised our voices of protest, our points of disagreement, with seriousness. We have always done so. But I think we are a bit more serious about completely obstructing the assembly. Yesterday... Therefore, in order to advance the assembly, the dignity of the National Assembly, the glory of the National Assembly, the guardianship of the National Assembly, which is spoken of in the entire intellectual and political sphere of Nepal, that the National Assembly has taken on a guardianship role in the entire political sphere of the country, within the federal parliament. To further elevate the role that the National Assembly has been playing, in this more suitable situation, in this difficult situation, which you are expressing. When I use your language. This difficult situation can be resolved by discussing and debating to move forward. This is my special request. Therefore, honorable members, let's sit down now.
(Slogan shouting by honorable members continues)
Honorable members, I inform you that this meeting of the National Assembly has been adjourned for 20 minutes.
(Thereafter, the meeting was adjourned for 20 minutes.)
Adjourned: 13:45 hrs.
The proceedings of the National Assembly meeting, adjourned for 20 minutes, commenced at 14:53 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honorable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the proceedings of the National Assembly meeting, which was adjourned today for 20 minutes
(14:53 hrs)
commence.
Slogan shouting by honorable members
Anti-national Prime Minister resign!
Resign! Resign!
Long live national pride!
Long live! Long live!
Uphold diplomatic dignity!
Uphold! Uphold!
Protect the border, respect the people!
Respect! Respect!
Let's uphold national unity!
Uphold! Uphold!
Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the issue for which the meeting was adjourned earlier, was that the same issue, or was there some other issue, honorable members? The slogans heard were all the same, repeated three times. Therefore, honorable members, the issues that you have raised in the assembly with seriousness. In terms of the subject matter, the way you have conveyed your voices through your medium at this time, it has drawn the attention of this assembly, of this assembly, including myself. This has happened in various ways during this period. The government's representative, the honorable minister, is also here. We have also discussed this in various ways. I don't see a solution emerging from just us sitting here, because I believe discussions have also taken place with the leaders of the parties, you sat amongst yourselves. What happened? I was told it was the same. I have nothing else to say. Therefore, repeating the same situation here will not lead to anything. Therefore, what needs to be done to move the process forward, I will also do that, I will also draw the government's attention from my position through various means and methods. Therefore, I specially request honorable members to cooperate in conducting the assembly.
Let's sit in our respective seats and move the house forward, move the assembly forward. Let's try to resolve this through other means, the issues you have raised are serious. I have also felt that. Therefore, let's try to resolve it through other means. My request to honorable members is to sit in your respective seats and let's proceed with today's proceedings.
I also want to mention here that the agenda item today was "Alternative Finance." It needs to be sent from here on the 29th. After presenting it, it requires 48 hours, 24 hours of time. We also have the responsibility to send it. It is also a somewhat special bill. Last time too, it got stuck here in a way. While we were considering it, the House of Representatives was dissolved, and then everything went wrong. It has come to us again, but if it gets stuck here, the general public... Since the alternative finance was a matter that was drawn up out of greater necessity by the previous government, it is also the responsibility of the National Assembly to move it forward, because it is not a controversial bill. It is a bill that has proceeded with consensus, it is an old bill. Therefore, we have to do that too. Our responsibility has increased a bit, and we have succeeded in giving the public outside a sense of responsibility in the National Assembly so far. It has been discussed. Whatever the House of Representatives may be, the National Assembly has maintained its prestige. It reflects the sentiments of the people of Nepal. We have maintained that prestige. I also realize that these issues of yours are also very serious in their own right. My attention has also been drawn to them. Therefore, I request that you sit down in your respective seats and cooperate in conducting the assembly.
(Slogan shouting by honorable members again)
Long live national pride!
Long live! Long live!
Let's uphold diplomatic dignity!
Uphold! Uphold!
Protect the border, respect the people!
Respect! Respect!
Let's uphold national unity!
Uphold! Uphold!
Anti-national Prime Minister resign!
Resign! Resign!
Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I again request you to cooperate in moving the assembly's work forward and to sit in your respective seats. I again request all honorable members to take their seats and cooperate in moving the assembly's work forward.
(Opposition by honorable members continues in the assembly)
Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, this meeting of the National Assembly will be adjourned until May 19, 2083, Wednesday, at 1:15 PM. This meeting is hereby adjourned.
(Thereafter, the next meeting was adjourned to be held on Wednesday, May 19, 2083, at 1:15 PM.)
Adjourned: 14:02 hrs.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The National Assembly meeting commenced at 13:22 hrs under the chairmanship of Narayan Prasad Dahal. The Chairperson announced that time would be allocated for urgent matters, with a maximum of three minutes per speaker.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Commencement of proceedings and allocation of time for urgent matters

sections.name: Urgent Time
sections.summary_en: Honourable members Ranjit Karna, Rajendra Laxmi Gaire, Ram Kumari Jhankri, and Tul Prasad Bishwakarma spoke during the urgent time, primarily criticizing the Prime Minister's statement regarding border encroachment by India and demanding clarification and an apology.

speakers.name: Ranjit Karna
speakers.topic: PM's statement on Indian border encroachment, demand for clarification and apology

speakers.name: Rajendra Laxmi Gaire
speakers.topic: Criticism of PM's statement favouring India, treasonous act

speakers.name: Ram Kumari Jhankri
speakers.topic: PM's statement causing shame, border encroachment, demand for investigation

speakers.name: Tul Prasad Bishwakarma
speakers.topic: PM's statement against national interest, demand for evidence of Nepal's encroachment

sections.name: Adjournment
sections.summary_en: Following the conclusion of urgent time, the Chairperson attempted to proceed with the scheduled agenda. However, members protested and chanted slogans, leading to a disruption of the proceedings.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The meeting commenced with slogan shouting by members regarding the Prime Minister's resignation, national pride, and diplomatic dignity. The Chairperson acknowledged the seriousness of the issues raised and urged members to cooperate in resuming the assembly proceedings.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Urging cooperation to resume assembly proceedings

sections.name: Adjournment
sections.summary_en: The National Assembly meeting was adjourned for 20 minutes due to ongoing slogan shouting by members. The meeting resumed later under the Chairperson's guidance.

sections.name: Resumption and Discussion
sections.summary_en: The Chairperson reconvened the meeting and addressed the persistent slogan shouting, acknowledging the members' concerns. He emphasized the need for dialogue and cooperation to resolve issues and move forward with the assembly's agenda, including the 'Alternative Finance' bill.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Addressing slogan shouting and urging cooperation

sections.name: Second Adjournment
sections.summary_en: Despite repeated requests from the Chairperson to resume proceedings, members continued their protest. The Chairperson announced the adjournment of the meeting until May 19, 2083, at 1:15 PM.
